CARD CATH
Cardiac Catheterization Report

Date of Birth: 3/11/1962   Gender: FEMALE
Height: 65(in)  Weight: 181.4(lb) BSA: 1.94
Procedure Date: 6/29/2026  Procedure Number: ACCHM000671
Cath Physician: Ullah, Waqas MD
Referring Physician: Gotimer, Patrick MD

History of Present Illness: 64 year old female presenting with inferior STEMI

The risks, benefits and alternatives of procedure were explained to the patient and
appropriate consent was obtained. The procedure was done in the Cath Lab under aseptic
technique using Lidocaine local anesthetic, appropriate guide wire, catheters, sheaths and
dilators. Following the procedure, the sheath(s) was/were removed and hemostasis was
obtained. Moderate sedation was given by interventional cardiologist and monitored by
trained independent observers for the duration of the procedure (including the first 15
minutes).

Procedure Name: Acute MI PCI, Coronary PTCA (initial), IVUS/OCT (initial), IVUS/OCT (addl)

ACCESS SITE: Sheath was inserted into the RIGHT radial artery

Left Main: No significant coronary artery disease.
LAD: 30% Mid lesion in LAD; 100% Proximal lesion in RCA
Circumflex: No significant coronary artery disease.
Right: 100% Proximal lesion in RCA, TIMI 0 flow pre-intervention

LV FINDINGS: Mildly elevated EDP pre angio
VALVE FINDINGS: No significant valvular disease

INTERVENTION:
Lesion Site #1 - Proximal right coronary artery segment - Pre stenosis 100%, post stenosis
10%. PRE TIMI flow 0, POST TIMI flow 3.

Estimated Total Blood Loss: 5 mL's
Complications: No Complications

Impression:
Total thrombotic occlusion of the proximal RCA causing inferior STEMI.
6F, Right radial access. JR4 6F guide, Runthrough wire. IVUS showing large thrombus burden
in the proximal RCA with reference vessel diameter of 3.5mm.
Severe proximal RCA stenosis s/p thrombectomy, IVUS guided 3.0mm compliant balloon
angioplasty, followed by 3.5x18mm XIENCE stent placement. Good final angiographic results
with TIMI 3 flow.

Post-procedure the patient was transferred to the cardiac recovery unit for extended
radial access site and hemodynamic monitoring per the post-PCI recovery protocol. The
following recovery flowsheet documents vital signs, access site checks, and neurovascular
checks performed at routine intervals during the recovery period.
